E070-01.notes: Nonessential appositive needs paired commas. B drops the closing comma (subject-verb split unevenly); C drops the opening comma; D mixes dash with comma.

E070-02.notes: Paragraph explains the overland relay; C supplies the transition from 'plane too risky' to sled. A is a trivial fact; B off-topic present-day; D generic history.

E070-03.notes: 'then afterward' is redundant; B still redundant; C wordier redundancy; D concise.

E070-04.notes: Sentence is about Seppala's biography, off the relay. A false (doesn't explain danger); C unsupported claim; D no contradiction.

E070-05.notes: Past narrative and 'had left' require simple past 'arrived'. A present, B future, D present perfect inconsistent with a dated past event.

E070-06.notes: Only D gives a reason (final leg into Nome) for Balto's fame. A says many dogs were famous (illogical with 'almost overnight' and doesn't explain); B time detail; C concession, no reason.

E070-07.notes: Sentence 11 links back to Togo/Seppala in paragraph 3. B no contradiction; C statue funding not mentioned; D Togo is mentioned earlier.

E070-08.notes: 'The ice there' needs an antecedent location with ice: Norton Sound in sentence 8. Others lack a referent for 'there' ice.

E070-09.notes: Only A contrasts 1925 with the race (trophy vs. lives). B, C, D give no contrast.

E070-10.notes: Essay explains need for serum and relay delivery. A/B mischaracterize focus; D false (sentence 3 explains why no plane).

E070-11.notes: A comma splice; B fused sentence; D 'which he began to wonder whether' is ungrammatical. C joins clauses with comma + and.

E070-12.notes: D gives concrete details (unmanned balloon, 30+ feet). A, B, C are vague.

E070-13.notes: Colon introduces the list after an independent clause. A comma makes list read as four items/ambiguous appositive; B semicolon needs independent clause after; D no punctuation.

E070-14.notes: Register: A, C, D are casual/slang; B is formal and precise.

E070-15.notes: Later museum history is off-topic. B, C false rationale; D no contradiction.

E070-16.notes: Dangling modifier: the risers must be the subject. A city rising; B the view rising; C 'below them' modifier with city as subject still dangles; D 'the two men' correct.

E070-17.notes: Redundancy: 'duration ... in length', 'minutes of time', 'period ... long' all redundant; B concise.

E070-18.notes: Chronology June -> Sept -> Nov 21 -> 'ten days later' (Charles). Current placement correct; moving it breaks dates and the 'ten days later' reference.

E070-19.notes: Paragraph is about Charles's hydrogen balloon, a rival design; C transitions. A isolated fact; B about Pilatre, not paragraph topic; D irrelevant.

E070-20.notes: Only D returns to Montgolfier's observation of the bag rising over a fire. A, B, C don't reference the first paragraph's observation.
